name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+18 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Colin Allred's $8 million raised and statewide name recognition
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 97%
Open seat after Crockett's retirement adds mild uncertainty
model.rationale: The Dallas-area district's D+18 lean, Allred's large fundraising advantage and high name recognition from his 2024 Senate run, and market pricing near 97% for Democrats all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat.
model.watch: A late surge in Republican fundraising or an unforeseen controversy involving Allred could narrow the margin, though the district's partisan fundamentals make an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's 33rd District, anchored in Dallas, leans Democratic by 18 points, and Jasmine Crockett's retirement to run for Senate leaves an open seat. Democrats nominated Colin Allred, a former congressman and 2024 Senate nominee with strong name recognition, while Republican Patrick Gillespie has reported little fundraising activity. The seat has been held by Democrats, and its partisan fundamentals strongly favor them.

Allred has raised over $8 million and holds a large financial advantage, with no outside spending against him. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent. No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, candidate resources, and market pricing. The combination points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the open-seat transition the main source of residual uncertainty.
